presentation.label: MIDI Retrig
presentation.summary: Use the native retrig menu on MIDI tracks A–H. Repeated notes follow the Digitakt sequencer, including chords, retrig rate, finite length and velocity changes.
presentation.overview: Use the native retrig menu on MIDI tracks A–H. Repeated notes follow the Digitakt sequencer, including chords, retrig rate, finite length and velocity changes.
highlights: Open the native retrig menu on a MIDI step.
Enable or disable retrig for the held step.
usage: Select MIDI track A with TRK + trig 9. Configure its MIDI channel for a connected synth and enter grid recording with RECORD.
Place a note trig. Hold that trig and press UP or DOWN to open RETRIG; turn A to enable it.
Choose RATE 1/32, a finite LEN and VEL 0. Release the trig and press PLAY to hear repeated MIDI notes.
Press STOP. To bypass this step, reopen its retrig menu and turn A to OFF.

access.location: MIDI track; grid recording; hold a trig and press UP or DOWN
steps: Select MIDI track A with TRK + trig 9. Configure its MIDI channel for a connected synth and enter grid recording with RECORD.

controls.name: Hold trig + UP/DOWN
controls.doc: Open the native retrig menu on a MIDI step.

controls.name: A — RETRIG
controls.doc: Enable or disable retrig for the held step.

controls.name: H — VEL
controls.doc: Set the velocity change across the retrig burst.

limitations: Requires an external MIDI destination to hear the result.
Dense chords at fast retrig rates increase MIDI traffic; hardware timing and downstream synth behavior need checking.

load.display: Adds 0.4% average, 6.5% worst-case of an audio block over stock (emulator)
load.conditions: Emulator: OS 1.53 on Core 2.1, 8 audio tracks triggering a full-scale sample and 8 MIDI tracks a note on every step at 120 BPM, 3,000 audio blocks timed with the MCF5441x instruction-timing model at 250 MHz, zero-wait memory. Module workload: retrig on all eight MIDI tracks at retrig rate index 16 and length 126. Stock: 59.1% average, 61.8% worst block. All six mods together: 73.2% worst block on 1.53, 73.3% on 1.54. Not a hardware measurement.

hardware.summary: sumedho reports the Core 2.1 all-mods builds fully tested and working on a Digitakt 1, OS 1.53 and 1.54, for about one to two hours in total, including project save and reload and a power cycle (2026-10-14): “ok fully tested on hardware and working”.
limitations: Duration is the reporter’s range (1–2 hours) for the combined session across both OS releases; recorded as 90 minutes.
Individual test outcomes were not itemized; standalone (single-mod) hardware coverage is not claimed.
Tested SysEx: 1.53 23503ca42478c1644dea5fd296893f628eafb6662d2ce5e291bfc591f045ae4e, 1.54 257144e4a584172e470c3dde83d7ccda636eeb195b4e5ff0492b3ebc8bdfaba2; firmware was not read back from the device.

tests.summary: Runs on Core 2.1. Emulator regressions on OS 1.53 and 1.54, an emulator CPU-load comparison with stock, and Modwerk source-build parity with the native build are in TESTING.md. sumedho reports this Core 2.1 build fully tested and working on a Digitakt 1, OS 1.53 and 1.54, for about one to two hours including project save/reload and a power cycle (2026-10-14).
